It isn't enforceable rule, just a guideline to prevent hostility and echochambers. If someone puts a lot of effort into writing a post that dissents on the majority then that person would be prevented from doing so in the future from doing it again because they would not feel welcome here. If we vote based on whether we agree or not, then those within the majority opinion would drive away those in the minority - leading to an echo chamber of the majority (see ShitRedditSays, CircleJerk or FatPeopleHate).

The point of a discussion should be to maximize insight into the issue being discussed by all participants and readers. People can just ignore this message, but in the long run it is beneficial to welcome dissenting and encourage dissenting opinions.
